messages:
maya: Quick sync — requirement: per-tenant routing policy that prefers regional model variants, but falls back gracefully when regional capacity is low. Also need a soft-quota enforcement mode that throttles/prefers cheaper variants before hard-denying. Thoughts?

jake: +1. We should expose an API shape and a console toggle. API needs to be explicit about 'preference vs hard-only' and a numeric soft quota threshold (e.g., 80%).

rachel: Runtime constraints: some quantized variants don't exist in every region. We need the policy to be able to declare compatible fallbacks (e.g., cpu-quant, int8-gpu). If fallback requires model format conversion we can't do that live — must be prebuilt.

tom: UX: in console show a small timeline preview of "expected route" and "fallback probability" given current metrics. Users should see what % traffic will hit fallback tier at current utilization. Minimal mock: a stacked bar with live estimate. :bar_chart:

lee: Infra note: regional pools have different instance types; we must let policy prefer by 'region+variant' weight, not just variant. Also add a circuit-breaker window so temporary spikes don't immediately flip variant.

alex: SRE perspective: we need SLOs for latency and error-rate per-variant so fallback decisions can be based on health, not only capacity. Also add a cooldown after failover.

quota-bot: [INFO] tenant:acme - 82% of soft quota for model:starlet-13b-int8 in us-west-2 (last 1h).

jake: Proposed API sketch (for review):
```
{
  "tier_policies": [
    {
      "tier": "free",
      "routes": [
        {"priority": 0, "region": "us", "variant": "starlet-7b-quant", "weight": 0.7},
        {"priority": 1, "region": "global", "variant": "starlet-7b-quant-cpu", "weight": 0.3}
      ],
      "soft_quota_pct": 75,
      "soft_mode": "prefers-cheaper-variants",
      "cooldown_secs": 300
    }
  ]
}
```

rachel: That looks fine. Two small asks: add "compatible_variants" list for each route (explicit map of safe fallbacks) and a boolean "allow_cross_region_fallback" so orgs can block sending data across regions.

maya: Agree. Also add telemetry hooks: for each decision record {selected_variant, reason: [capacity|health|policy], pre_percentile_latency}. We need to feed those into Optimize later.

jake: Console language: avoid calling it "soft quota" to customers — call it "degrade threshold" and an explanation: "When usage passes X% the platform will prefer lower-cost compatible variants until load normalizes."

tom: UX nit: when users toggle degrade threshold, show an impact estimate for last 24h (how much would have hit fallbacks). Quick compute on preview helps adoption.

lee: Implementation notes: we'll need a scheduler change to score route candidates by composite score: weighted_capacity_score * policy_weight + health_score * alpha + region_pref_bonus. We can tune alpha per-tenant.

alex: For rollouts, add a route-level canary flag: 'canary_pct' to route small % to a new variant and measure latency/regressions before expanding. Keep canary independent from degrade behavior.

maya: Action items: 1) jake + rachel to finalize API shape incl compatible_variants + allow_cross_region_fallback (due EOD Wed). 2) lee to prototype scoring function (POC lambda) by next week. 3) tom to mock console preview and impact calc. 4) alex to design SLO tags for variants.

jake: One more: we should keep policy authoring both in flat JSON and a readable Console editor; mappings should be lossless. Also record policy versions for rollbacks.

maya: OK — I'll make a brief ADR draft after we finalize fields. If no objections I'll create a PR with API proto tomorrow. :memo:

rachel: no objections. small concern: ensure we don't add expensive per-request checks; the scoring must be cacheable.

lee: noted. use windowed metrics + cached route decisions for TTL=1s.

maya: thanks all. I'll post the PR link once created and tag reviewers. :rocket:
